experiment_title: Zero-Day Attack Simulation via Held-Out Attack Category Protocol
protocol_description: Models are evaluated on attack categories strictly excluded from training data to simulate real-world zero-day network threats.

held_out_categories.analysis: Evaluated on 5 real instances of 'PortScan'. Isolation Forest detected 5/5 via unsupervised divergence.
Evaluated on 2 real instances of 'Infiltration'. Isolation Forest detected 2/2 via unsupervised divergence.
Evaluated on 2 real instances of 'Botnet'. Isolation Forest detected 2/2 via unsupervised divergence.

overall_summary.academic_conclusion: Supervised classifiers trained only on known attacks show lower recall on novel topologies. The unsupervised Isolation Forest achieved 100.0% detection on held-out attacks without seeing their labels.

limitations: An anomaly is not automatically a confirmed zero-day vulnerability; it denotes a statistically significant divergence from normal traffic distributions.
High network throughput fluctuations and sudden flash crowds can cause temporary false-positive spikes.
Sophisticated low-and-slow stealth attacks that intentionally mimic benign flow statistics remain challenging for statistical isolation.
